question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=y(t)+(x(t)-2)^{3}+8 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)+4+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y(t)+8)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the behavior of the system's solutions near the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[2,\text{ }-8]^{T}?$

$\,$
The equilibrium is an 
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}y+(x-2)^{3}+8 \\ -2x+4+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+8)\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $\text{\boldsymbol}f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y+(x-2)^{3}+8)=3(x-2)^{2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2x(t)+4+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y(t)+8))=1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2x+4+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+8))=-2 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2x(t)+4+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y(t)+8))=\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+8)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3(x-2)^{2} & 1 \\ -2 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(y+8)\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[2,\text{ }-8]^{T}$ to get

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}3((2)-2)^{2} & 1 \\ -2 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(-8+8)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-\lambda +2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=\frac{1}{2}\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}i.$

Since we have two complex eigenvalues with positive real parts, our equilibrium is an $\text{unstable}$ $\text{spiral source}.$
